sehemu: Part I: Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance
jina: Functions of the Commission and procedures for implementation
maudhui: (1) The Commission for Human Rights and Good Governance shall perform the following functions: (a) promote within the country the protection of human rights and duties to society in accordance with the Constitution and laws of the land; (b) receive complaints concerning violations of human rights generally; (c) conduct inquiries into matters involving violations of human rights and contravention of principles of good governance; (d) conduct research and provide and disseminate public education concerning human rights and good governance; (e) where necessary, institute proceedings in court to prevent violations of human rights or to restore rights arising from such violations or contravention of principles of good governance; (f) inquire into the conduct of any person or institution concerned with this Article in the ordinary exercise or abuse of the powers or duties of office; (g) advise the Government and other public and private-sector organs on human rights and good governance; and (h) take appropriate action to promote and facilitate conciliation and settlement among persons and institutions appearing before the Commission. (2) The Commission shall be an autonomous department and, without prejudice to the other provisions of this Article, in exercising its powers under this Constitution it shall not be bound to comply with directions or orders of any person or Government department, or the views of any political party or other public or private institution. (3) Subarticle (2) shall not be construed as preventing the President from giving directions or orders to the Commission, nor as entitling the Commission to disregard them where the President considers that the national interest so requires. (4) The Commission shall conduct inquiries in accordance with this Article and a law enacted by Parliament, shall inquire whenever directed by the President, and, unless directed by the President not to do so, may conduct an inquiry whenever it considers it appropriate. (5) The Commission shall have no jurisdiction to inquire into a decision of a Judge, Magistrate or court made in the exercise of judicial authority, nor a decision of any quasi-judicial body established by law made in the exercise of its jurisdiction. (6) This Article shall apply to employees of the Government of the United Republic and Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar, employees and leaders of political parties dealing with public affairs, members and employees of Government commissions, public corporations and other private bodies as prescribed by law, but shall not apply to the President or the Head of the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar except subject to Article 46 of this Constitution or Article 36 of the Constitution of Zanzibar, 1984.

(2) The Commission shall be an autonomous department and, without prejudice to the other provisions of this Article, in exercising its powers under this Constitution it shall not be bound to comply with directions or orders of any person or Government department, or the views of any political party or other public or private institution.
